title: Model packing: runtime impact of lossy model compression on throughput, tails, and embeddings
content:
Goal:
- Quick exploration: can we pack multiple quantized variants into a single on-disk artifact/container and what is the live-serving cost (throughput, p95/p99, and quality regressions)?

Motivation / context:
- Customers want smaller images and fewer artifacts to manage across Dedicated fleets. Packaging multiple quantized flavor blobs (fp16, int8, awq, gptq) into one artifact could simplify rollouts. But runtime behavior might suffer: memory layout changes, page faults, kernel selection jitter, KV cache alignment issues.
- This is a lightweight field experiment to collect signal before a larger infra change. Not exhaustive.

Hypotheses (quick):
1) Packing increases cold-start and warmup costs due to larger mmap regions and relocation work; steady-state throughput mostly unchanged for single-variant requests.
2) Mixed-workload traffic hitting different kernels (AWQ vs GPTQ) will increase scheduler jitter and p99 latency due to kernel occupancy switching.
3) Embedding output (cosine similarity) will have small drops for AWQ/GPTQ on some corpora; int8 shows occasional outlier failures on math-like prompts.

Setup / methodology:
- Models tested: Llama2-13B base near-fp16, int8-GPTQ, AWQ-8bit, simulated FP8 (tooling-run conversion).
- Artifact packaging: created single tarball with four weight blobs + small manifest; runtime memory maps each blob on first use.
- Hardware: NVIDIA A10G and A40 nodes (same infra as staging).
- Workloads: short-chat (avg 40 tokens), long-context summarization (avg 1200 tokens), embeddings (512-d cosine). Mixed traffic mixes 80% chat + 20% embeddings.
- Metrics captured: throughput (req/s), latency p50/p95/p99, GPU memory usage, host RSS, page-faults/sec, KV cache hit ratio, token-level perplexity, embedding cosine similarity to fp16 baseline, instruction-following score (simple rubric, 0-1).
- Measurement windows: cold-start (first 10 requests after restart), warm (minutes 5-15), steady-state (15-60m under steady QPS), burst (sustained 3x normal QPS for 120s).

Key results (summary lines from runs):
- Cold start overhead (first generate) per-node: +420ms median vs single-variant deploy; page faults spiked x12. More pronounced on A10G.
- Warmup: 95th latency baseline fp16 220ms -> packed artifact 320ms (+45%). After 30s of continuous traffic, gap shrinks to ~+10%.
- Steady-state throughput (chat single-variant traffic): negligible difference (<3% drop) when requests consistently hit same quantized variant.
- Mixed-kernel jitter: p99 jump from 720ms (single-variant) to 1.3s under mixed AWQ/GPTQ traffic. Observed kernel switch cost ~150-350ms depending on batchshape.
- Embedding fidelity: AWQ mean cosine to fp16 baseline 0.997 on semantic-sim dataset, but 0.92 on short-term entity disambiguation set (indicator of brittle tokens). GPTQ int8: 0.994 overall, but outliers with cosine <0.85 on numeric-heavy docs.
- Instruction-following (hand-eval 200 prompts): fp16 baseline 0.88, AWQ 0.82 (drop concentrated in multi-step reasoning), GPTQ 0.85, int8 0.79 (edge cases).

Representative raw table (text):
MODEL    | QPS(chat) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | emb-cos-mean | inst-follow
fp16     | 18.6      | 330     | 720     | 1.000        | 0.88
GPTQ-int8| 19.1      | 350     | 760     | 0.994        | 0.85
AWQ-8bit | 18.9      | 380     | 1300    | 0.997        | 0.82
int8-pack| 17.8      | 420     | 1400    | 0.992        | 0.79

Operational notes / interesting signals:
- mmap fragmentation: when multiple blobs mapped, resident set layout causes more syscalls on first page touches. Observed higher minor-fault counts. Potential mitigations: pre-touch warmup, bundling manifest ordering to map hot variant first.
- Kernel cache thrash: our scheduler keeps kernel-specific caches (workspace allocators) cold when we switch variant frequently. This maps to the p99 jumps above. Consider per-kernel prewarming or affinity-based routing.
- Prefix/KV cache alignment: mixed variants that use different KV formats cause eviction pressure. When embedding traffic interleaves with generation, we see KV hit ratio drop ~8% and subsequent latency uplift.
- Compression side-effects: packaging with LZ4 reduces tarball size by x3, but runtime decompression during first map adds ~200–400ms. We could store compressed blobs but pre-decompress at image-install time.

Failure modes observed:
- Numeric-destructive prompts: some int8/GPTQ conversions produced incorrect arithmetic outputs; reproducible to certain weight groups (not random). Logged and linked under JIRA-INF-2378.
- Tokenization edge drift: AWQ produced shifted token-generation for OOV tokens in a small % of runs. Likely quant-residual error. Needs fuzzing suite.

Quick experiments we ran to probe root causes:
- Mapped only header + hot-blob strategy: reordering manifest to ensure the actively-served variant is mapped first reduced cold-start by ~200ms.
- Per-kernel allocator warmup: calling a no-op generation on each kernel during warmup reduced p99 jumps by ~30% in mixed traffic.
- Embedding isolation: moving embeddings to a dedicated route (separate worker pool) removed KV eviction artifacts entirely.

Open questions / next steps:
- Is the operational win of fewer artifacts worth the steady-state tail penalties for mixed-tenant fleets? Need cost model: SLO breach cost vs storage/ops savings.
- Can we implement lazy-sparse prefetching that touches only hot pages, but sequences them in background so first-request penalty disappears?
- How well do these signals generalize across heavier models (70B) and on different architectures (H100)?
- Should deployment tooling recommend manifest ordering or enforce it? Add a packing lint rule?
- Run longer A/B for 48h with production-like burst patterns and instrument kernel occupancy and GPU SM utilization at sub-second granularity.

Action items / tickets:
- INF-2378: catalog numeric-destructive prompts + weight-group mapping (assigned Diego).
- PR #842: add manifest-ordering helper and pre-touch option (work-in-progress).
- INF-2399: schedule 48h mixed-traffic run on A40 + H100 matrix (owner: Tom).
- Add embedding route isolation experiment to canary checklist (owner: Rachel).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Could be a default "packed artifact" mode for low-risk customers (embedding-only fleets). For mixed-generation fleets, default to single variant per image.
- Consider a packaging tool that calculates a hotness score per blob and writes an order optimized for page locality.
- Instrumentation gap: need per-kernel microsecond metrics visible in Console (SM occupancy, kernel load/unload time).

Appendix: quick command snippets used
- build pack: ./packager --model ll2-13b --variants fp16,gptq,awq,int8 --out /tmp/pack.tar.lz4
- run profiling: ./bench-client --target staging:8080 --profile --mix "chat:80,embed:20" --dur 3600 
- perf sample: nsys profile --output run1.nsys --trace=nvtx --duration 3600 \

References / links in notes:
- JIRA-INF-2378 (numeric-destructive prompts)
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/842 (manifest-ordering helper)
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime thread ts:1659341223

Status / recommendation (draft):
- Do not roll packed artifacts to mixed-production fleets yet. Try embedding-only customers or low-SLA workloads. Implement manifest-ordering and per-kernel warmup in the runtime first.
- Continue experiments: 48h mixed-run, measure cost delta from p99 breaches.

-- Aisha
